comparison: Perfect agreement on simulation predictions (C4, C5, C22, C23, C59-C62). Both evaluations find the computational approach convincing and well-supported. OpenEval emphasizes methodological details and robustness testing, while peer reviewers highlight the systematic combination of simulations with experiments.

Strong agreement on experimental findings (C25-C31, C63-C64). Both evaluations endorse the mixed nucleotide experimental approach. OpenEval provides detailed statistical validation (P<0.001, sample sizes), while peer reviewers affirm the convincing nature of the approach without questioning data quality.

Complete agreement on super-stoichiometric poisoning effect (C34-C37). Both evaluations accept the differential behavior at plus- vs minus-ends. OpenEval emphasizes how observations match simulation predictions, while peer reviewers highlight novel insights about cap structure.

Full agreement on main conclusion (C6, C9, C47, C55). All three peer reviewers explicitly endorse the interface-acting mechanism, matching OpenEval's assessment that evidence strongly supports this conclusion through convergence of multiple lines of evidence.

Agreement on mosaic cap model implications (C48, C49, C51, C54). Both evaluations support the broader conceptual advance. OpenEval notes consistency with literature, while peer reviewers explicitly highlight novel insights about cap structure.

Agreement on nucleotide exchange mechanism (C8, C45, C46). Both evaluations accept the resolution of quantitative discrepancy through exchange parameter. OpenEval provides detailed validation against literature values, while peer reviewers implicitly accept through overall endorsement.

Partial overlap on poisoning mechanism (C7, C43, C44 in OpenEval vs C7, C34-C37 in peer). Both support the mechanistic explanation. OpenEval focuses on the super-stoichiometric mechanism details, while peer reviewers emphasize the overall poisoning interpretation.

Agreement on model fitting and baseline behavior (C38-C42). Both evaluations accept the modeling approach. OpenEval explicitly notes the acknowledged discrepancy at plus-end as strengthening transparency, while peer reviewers accept the overall modeling without critique.

Agreement on binding affinity measurements (C32, C33). Both evaluations support the convergence of kinetic and direct binding measurements. OpenEval emphasizes methodological validation, while peer reviewers accept parameter fitting without objection.

Divergent assessment of speculative claims (C52, C53, C58). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting speculation lacks direct experimental support. Peer reviewers do not challenge these speculations, suggesting implicit acceptance, though without explicit endorsement.

Divergent assessment of evolutionary speculation (C56-C58). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the broad evolutionary hypothesis extends beyond study scope. Peer reviewers do not object to speculation, but also do not explicitly endorse it.

OpenEval evaluates background/context claims (C1, C10-C21, C24, C50) as SUPPORTED, noting they represent established knowledge appropriately cited. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate background claims.
OpenEval evaluates definitional claims (C2, C3) as SUPPORTED, noting clear definitions of competing models. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate these foundational definitions.
